chunks: From him, from Hammad, from Hariz, who said: Zayd al-Shahham, Zurarah, and Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated to me from Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام that he said:

If something of madhy or wadhy flows from your private part, then do not wash it, do not break the salat (prayer) for it, and do not invalidate the wudu (ablution) because of it. It is only in the position of phlegm. Everything that comes out of you after the wudu (ablution), then it is from the residual passages.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: the ritual prayer, which is not to be interrupted because of this discharge
key_terms.النُّخَامَةِ: phlegm, used as a comparison to show the discharge is legally negligible
key_terms.الْحَبَائِلِ: the residual passages or remaining channels from which such discharge emerges
key_terms.الْوُضُوءَ: ritual ablution, which is not invalidated by this discharge
key_terms.مَذْيٍ: a thin discharge mentioned here as not invalidating ritual purity
key_terms.وَذْيٍ: a discharge mentioned alongside madhy with the same ruling here

ai.seo_question: Does madhy or wadhy invalidate wudu (ablution) or break salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that the discharge known as madhy or wadhy does not require washing, does not interrupt salat (prayer), and does not invalidate wudu (ablution). The Imam عليه السلام likens it to phlegm, indicating its legal insignificance in ritual purity after wudu (ablution).
